evidence_summary: InterFax Electronics was a small Milwaukee-area electronics repair business operated by Ed Giese that also produced a very small run of instrument-effect pedals. The HP-1 Harmonic Percolator is directly documented as an InterFax product, with later historical sources consistently attributing the pedal to Giese. The archive should preserve InterFax as the builder identity and keep later Harmonic Percolator reproductions and trademark holders as separate successor/relationship records.

evidence_summary: Sandro Marchetti's historical interview identifies MET (Micro Elettro Tecnica) of Carlo Baldoni as an early electronics and mechanical supplier whose lineage fed into Logan, G.I.S. and later EF-EL work. This is important historical manufacturing infrastructure, but the current evidence does not justify treating MET itself as a discrete commercial dirt-pedal builder. Preserve it as a research-only predecessor/relationship node until specific pedal products are tied to the company.

ToneHome documents Kent Model 6406 The Angry Fuzz as made in Germany and officially released at Musikmesse Frankfurt in 1971. The surviving evidence establishes a real period marketed product but does not yet securely identify the physical factory, so Kent remains a marketed/product node pending factory attribution.
